title: Minimum One Bit Operations to Make Integers Zero
summary: For an integer n, apply operations to convert it to zero by flipping the least significant bit or a bit if the preceding bit is one and all preceding bits are zero.
statement: For an integer n, apply operations to convert it to zero by flipping the least significant bit or a bit if the preceding bit is one and all preceding bits are zero. The goal is to find the fewest operations needed.
constraints: Use only the stated constrained bit flips and return the minimum operations needed to reach zero.
hints: The allowed moves follow reflected Gray-code order.
Invert a Gray-coded value by XORing all of its right-shifted prefixes.
Repeatedly XOR n into the answer and shift n right until zero.
Each XOR prefix reconstructs one binary bit of the operation index, yielding the unique shortest position of n in the Gray path to zero.
editorial: Each XOR prefix reconstructs one binary bit of the operation index, yielding the unique shortest position of n in the Gray path to zero.

tests.explanation: The sequence 3 to 1 to 0 uses two valid operations.
The minimum valid sequence requires four operations.
